Amy / Soojin — thanks, I reviewed the BrightCorps redlines and attached a short counsel memo + redline-summary. High-level positions below (we can convert these into tracked edits once you confirm):

1) Subprocessors: Redwood will maintain a public subprocessor inventory and provide 30 days' notice prior to adding a new subprocessor. We cannot provide pre-approval for every analytics vendor but will honor a prior notice + objection process for customers with legitimate compliance concerns. Suggested clause: "Customer may object in writing within 30 days of notice; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to address objection."

2) Transfers: For EU-related data, Redwood accepts SCCs (2021 modules) or equivalent addendum. We will not unilaterally change transfer mechanism and will bind subprocessors to the same safeguards. Proposed language: "Standard Contractual Clauses or other lawful transfer mechanism as agreed in writing."

3) Retention: We cannot agree to a blanket 7-year retention for logs. Proposed approach: customer-specific retention controls in the SOW with default retention of 90 days for detailed logs and 12 months for aggregated telemetry. We will support longer retention by mutual agreement.

4) Audit rights: We agree to a single, on-site or remote audit per year with reasonable scope and prior notice; for security-sensitive areas we prefer an independent third-party SOC/ISO report in lieu of onsite audits.

5) KV cache / telemetry: Aditya — please confirm technical treatment. My view: KV cache for active inference state is ephemeral and part of runtime; aggregated usage telemetry is platform telemetry and not a subprocessor activity. If BrightCorps needs export of cache state, that's a different discussion.

Attachment: DPA_Redline_annotated.pdf (summary + proposed language). If BrightCorps is ok with SCCs, we will prepare a tracked-change counter and aim to send for eSign by end of week.

Monica Patel | Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
